entrypoints.summary: Authenticated GET /api/<path:subpath> passes route-controlled subpath to get_target before listing, decoding a file, or executing an .exe.
Authenticated PUT /api/<path:subpath> passes route-controlled subpath to get_target before creating directories, files, or symlinks.
Authenticated DELETE /api/<path:subpath> passes route-controlled subpath to get_target before recursive removal or unlinking.

affected_components.role: Resolves API-controlled paths, performs the containment decision, and dispatches filesystem operations.

causal_paths.kind: HTTP route subpath to resolved target authorization and filesystem sink

preconditions: The client has a session containing the token set by the index route.
A resolved sibling-prefix path is available such that it passes the character-prefix comparison; availability and reachability of a protected resource are not demonstrated.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: A route subpath that resolves outside the token directory but shares its character prefix.
trigger_steps.summary: Send an authenticated API request whose subpath resolves to a candidate textual-prefix sibling path, causing the handler to invoke get_target.

capabilities.concept: filesystem operations on an accepted resolved out-of-jail target

relation_candidates.rationale: API route subpath is client-controlled and is passed to get_target, whose resolved-target authorization uses a character-prefix comparison.

relation_candidates.dst: filesystem operations on an accepted resolved out-of-jail target
relation_candidates.rationale: Once get_target returns an accepted target, GET, PUT, and DELETE act on it through read/list/run, create, and removal operations.
The handlers are intended to work below a token-specific base path, but an accepted non-descendant sibling-prefix target would be outside that boundary.
relation_candidates.src: filesystem operations on an accepted resolved out-of-jail target

relation_candidates.rationale: A descendant check based on resolved path components would reject a sibling that merely shares the base directory's text prefix.

impact.affected_asset: Per-session filesystem-jail boundary rooted at C:\Temp\<token>; no particular external file or flag is evidenced as reached.
impact.attacker_capability: Cause GET, PUT, or DELETE handlers to operate on an accepted resolved sibling-prefix path rather than a verified descendant of the caller's token directory.
impact.security_effect: Potential execution of supported filesystem operations outside the intended per-token directory, limited to resolved paths that pass the textual-prefix predicate.

causal_trace.summary: An HTTP client holding the Flask session token can supply the API route subpath; each API handler forwards it to get_target.

get_target resolves base_path / path but authorizes the resolved target with os.path.commonprefix, which compares a textual prefix rather than path components; a sibling resolved path whose name begins with the token-directory text can satisfy this comparison without being a descendant.

After the character-prefix predicate accepts the target, the API performs target-dependent filesystem operations: GET reads/list files or runs .exe files, PUT creates objects, and DELETE removes objects.

The intended token-directory filesystem boundary can be bypassed for an accepted resolved sibling-prefix path, allowing the selected API operation to act on that accepted target. The supplied artifacts do not demonstrate access to another token directory, the excluded flag executable, or another protected resource.

failure.operation: Authorization of a resolved API filesystem target using os.path.commonprefix instead of a component-aware descendant check.

primary_invariant.statement: Every resolved API target must be a descendant of the requesting session's base path under C:\Temp\<token>.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The implementation treats a character-level common prefix equal to the base-path string as evidence of containment, which does not establish that the resolved target is beneath that path as a filesystem component.

quality.review_notes: The primary server source directly establishes the route-to-resolution-to-commonprefix control flow and subsequent filesystem sinks. No supplied request/response trace, exploit, test result, or patch proves a practical collision path or access to another principal's data, C:\exes\flag.exe, or a real flag; those impacts remain unclaimed.

remediation.invariant_restored: Authorize a resolved target only when it is a true descendant of the resolved per-token base directory, rejecting textual-prefix siblings before any read, write, execution, or deletion operation.

state_context.attacker_state_setup: Obtain the session established by the index route, then issue authenticated API requests containing a chosen route subpath.
data_structure_invariants: The token-specific base path is intended to delimit all resolved filesystem targets for that session.
API operations should occur only after target authorization.
state_context.state_machine: A visit to / establishes a session token; token_required then permits API handlers, and get_target creates that token's base directory on first use.

target.component: Flask filesystem API and per-session token storage
